request: Body myths: true or myth? Cracking knuckles, swallowed spiders, shaved hair, the senses, the stomach. #interactive #short
subtitle: Five things people say about your body, from cracked knuckles to swallowed spiders: true or myth? Guess each one, then hear the story behind it.

sources.title: Does knuckle cracking lead to arthritis of the fingers?
sources.finding: one man cracked the knuckles of his left hand, not his right, for over 60 years: no arthritis in either; Ig Nobel Prize in Medicine 2009

sources.title: The effect of shaving on the growth of hair
sources.finding: shaving did not change the colour, coarseness or rate of growth of hair

sources.title: Anatomy and Physiology: The Stomach
sources.finding: the stomach's surface epithelial cells are replaced every 3 to 5 days

commands.speak: Your body, true or myth? First, Grandma’s favourite warning: cracking your knuckles gives you arthritis.

quiz.question: Cracking your knuckles gives you arthritis. True or myth?
quiz.right: Myth. A doctor, Donald Unger, cracked the knuckles of one hand for sixty years and never the other: no arthritis in either, and an Ig Nobel Prize.

commands.speak: Next, the one that ruins bedtime: we all swallow spiders in our sleep.

quiz.question: We swallow spiders in our sleep. True or myth?
quiz.right: Myth. No case has ever been recorded, and a big, breathing, rumbling sleeper is the last place a spider wants to go.

commands.speak: Then the razor’s old reputation: shave, and the hair grows back thicker.

quiz.question: Shaved hair grows back thicker. True or myth?
quiz.right: Myth. The razor leaves a blunt tip that feels coarse, but a study in 1928 already found the hair grows back no thicker and no faster.

commands.speak: Now a school lesson: you have more than five senses.

quiz.question: Humans have more than five senses. True or myth?
quiz.right: True. Balance, heat, pain, and knowing where your arms are with your eyes shut are senses too: scientists count far more than five.

commands.speak: And last, a strange one: your stomach gets a new lining every few days.

quiz.question: Your stomach lining renews itself every few days. True or myth?
quiz.right: True. The cells on the stomach's surface are replaced every three to five days, before its own acid can digest them.

commands.speak: The three family warnings were myths. The two from biology class were true.

feedback.perfect: Your body has no secrets from you.
feedback.good: A sharp eye for an old wives' tale.
